bsb.11:24: So Moses went out and relayed to the people the words of the LORD, and he gathered seventy of the elders of the people and had them stand around the tent.
bsb.11:25: Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and He took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and placed that Spirit on the seventy elders. As the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied—but they never did so again.
bsb.11:26: Two men, however, had remained in the camp—one named Eldad and the other Medad—and the Spirit rested on them. They were among those listed, but they had not gone out to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp.
bsb.11:27: A young man ran and reported to Moses, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”
bsb.11:28: Joshua son of Nun, the attendant to Moses since youth, spoke up and said, “Moses, my lord, stop them!”
bsb.11:29: But Moses replied, “Are you jealous on my account? I wish that all the LORD’s people were prophets and that the LORD would place His Spirit on them!”
bsb.11:30: Then Moses returned to the camp, along with the elders of Israel.
bsb.11:31: Now a wind sent by the LORD came up, drove in quail from the sea, and brought them near the camp, about two cubits above the surface of the ground, for a day’s journey in every direction around the camp.
bsb.11:32: All that day and night, and all the next day, the people stayed up gathering the quail. No one gathered less than ten homers, and they spread them out all around the camp.
bsb.11:33: But while the meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed, the anger of the LORD burned against the people, and the LORD struck them with a severe plague.
bsb.11:34: So they called that place Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved other food.
bsb.11:35: From Kibroth-hattaavah the people moved on to Hazeroth, where they remained for some time.
bsb.12:1: Then Miriam and Aaron criticized Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married, for he had taken a Cushite wife.
bsb.12:2: “Does the LORD speak only through Moses?” they said. “Does He not also speak through us?” And the LORD heard this.
bsb.12:3: Now Moses was a very humble man, more so than any man on the face of the earth.
bsb.12:4: And suddenly the LORD said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, “You three, come out to the Tent of Meeting.” So the three went out,
bsb.12:5: and the LORD came down in a pillar of cloud, stood at the entrance to the Tent, and summoned Aaron and Miriam. When both of them had stepped forward,
bsb.12:6: He said, “Hear now My words: If there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, will reveal Myself to him in a vision; I will speak to him in a dream.
bsb.12:7: But this is not so with My servant Moses; he is faithful in all My house.
bsb.12:8: I speak with him face to face, clearly and not in riddles; he sees the form of the LORD. Why then were you unafraid to speak against My servant Moses?”
bsb.12:9: So the anger of the LORD burned against them, and He departed.
bsb.12:10: As the cloud lifted from above the Tent, suddenly Miriam became leprous, white as snow. Aaron turned toward her, saw that she was leprous,
bsb.12:11: and said to Moses, “My lord, please do not hold against us this sin we have so foolishly committed.
bsb.12:12: Please do not let her be like a stillborn infant whose flesh is half consumed when he comes out of his mother’s womb.”
bsb.12:13: So Moses cried out to the LORD, “O God, please heal her!”
bsb.12:14: But the LORD answered Moses, “If her father had but spit in her face, would she not have been in disgrace for seven days? Let her be confined outside the camp for seven days; after that she may be brought back in.”
bsb.12:15: So Miriam was confined outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not move on until she was brought in again.
bsb.12:16: After that, the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the Wilderness of Paran.
bsb.13:1: And the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.13:2: “Send out for yourself men to spy out the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites. From each of their fathers’ tribes send one man who is a leader among them.”
bsb.13:3: So at the consent of the LORD, Moses sent them out from the Wilderness of Paran. All the men were leaders of the Israelites,
bsb.13:4: and these were their names: From the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;
bsb.13:5: from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;
bsb.13:6: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
bsb.13:7: from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
bsb.13:8: from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
bsb.13:9: from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
bsb.13:10: from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
bsb.13:11: from the tribe of Manasseh (a tribe of Joseph), Gaddi son of Susi;
bsb.13:12: from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
bsb.13:13: from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;
bsb.13:14: from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;
bsb.13:15: and from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.
bsb.13:16: These were the names of the men Moses sent to spy out the land; and Moses gave to Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua.
bsb.13:17: When Moses sent them to spy out the land of Canaan, he told them, “Go up through the Negev and into the hill country.
bsb.13:18: See what the land is like and whether its people are strong or weak, few or many.
bsb.13:19: Is the land where they live good or bad? Are the cities where they dwell open camps or fortifications?
bsb.13:20: Is the soil fertile or unproductive? Are there trees in it or not? Be courageous, and bring back some of the fruit of the land.” (It was the season for the first ripe grapes.)
bsb.13:21: So they went up and spied out the land from the Wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, toward Lebo-hamath.
bsb.13:22: They went up through the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, dwelled. It had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.
bsb.13:23: When they came to the Valley of Eshcol, they cut down a branch with a single cluster of grapes, which they carried on a pole between two men. They also took some pomegranates and figs.
bsb.13:24: Because of the cluster of grapes the Israelites cut there, that place was called the Valley of Eshcol.
bsb.13:25: After forty days the men returned from spying out the land,
bsb.13:26: and they went back to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation of Israel in the Wilderness of Paran at Kadesh. They brought back a report for the whole congregation and showed them the fruit of the land.
bsb.13:27: And they gave this account to Moses: “We went into the land to which you sent us, and indeed, it is flowing with milk and honey. Here is some of its fruit!
bsb.13:28: Nevertheless, the people living in the land are strong, and the cities are large and fortified. We even saw the descendants of Anak there.
bsb.13:29: The Amalekites live in the land of the Negev; the Hittites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hill country; and the Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan.”
bsb.13:30: Then Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said, “We must go up and take possession of the land, for we can certainly conquer it!”
bsb.13:31: But the men who had gone up with him replied, “We cannot go up against the people, for they are stronger than we are!”
bsb.13:32: So they gave the Israelites a bad report about the land that they had spied out: “The land we explored devours its inhabitants, and all the people we saw there are great in stature.
bsb.13:33: We even saw the Nephilim there—the descendants of Anak that come from the Nephilim! We seemed like grasshoppers in our own sight, and we must have seemed the same to them!”
bsb.14:1: Then the whole congregation lifted up their voices and cried out, and that night the people wept.
bsb.14:2: All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole congregation said to them, “If only we had died in the land of Egypt, or if only we had died in this wilderness!
bsb.14:3: Why is the LORD bringing us into this land to fall by the sword? Our wives and children will become plunder. Would it not be better for us to go back to Egypt?”
bsb.14:4: So they said to one another, “Let us appoint a leader and return to Egypt.”
bsb.14:5: Then Moses and Aaron fell facedown before the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel.
bsb.14:6: Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had spied out the land, tore their clothes
bsb.14:7: and said to the whole congregation of Israel, “The land we passed through and explored is an exceedingly good land.
bsb.14:8: If the LORD delights in us, He will bring us into this land, a land flowing with milk and honey, and He will give it to us.
bsb.14:9: Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not be afraid of the people of the land, for they will be like bread for us. Their protection has been removed, and the LORD is with us. Do not be afraid of them!”
bsb.14:10: But the whole congregation threatened to stone Joshua and Caleb. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to all the Israelites at the Tent of Meeting.
bsb.14:11: And the LORD said to Moses, “How long will this people treat Me with contempt? How long will they refuse to believe in Me, despite all the signs I have performed among them?
bsb.14:12: I will strike them with a plague and destroy them—and I will make you into a nation greater and mightier than they are.”
bsb.14:13: But Moses said to the LORD, “The Egyptians will hear of it, for by Your strength You brought this people from among them.
bsb.14:14: And they will tell it to the inhabitants of this land. They have already heard that You, O LORD, are in the midst of this people, that You, O LORD, have been seen face to face, that Your cloud stands over them, and that You go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
bsb.14:15: If You kill this people as one man, the nations who have heard of Your fame will say,
bsb.14:16: ‘Because the LORD was unable to bring this people into the land He swore to give them, He has slaughtered them in the wilderness.’
bsb.14:17: So now I pray, may the power of my Lord be magnified, just as You have declared:
bsb.14:18: ‘The LORD is slow to anger and abounding in loving devotion, forgiving iniquity and transgression. Yet He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished; He will visit the iniquity of the fathers upon their children to the third and fourth generation.’
bsb.14:19: Pardon, I pray, the iniquity of this people, in keeping with the greatness of Your loving devotion, just as You have forgiven them ever since they left Egypt.”
bsb.14:20: “I have pardoned them as you requested,” the LORD replied.
bsb.14:21: “Yet as surely as I live and as surely as the whole earth is filled with the glory of the LORD,
bsb.14:22: not one of the men who have seen My glory and the signs I performed in Egypt and in the wilderness—yet have tested Me and disobeyed Me these ten times—
bsb.14:23: not one will ever see the land that I swore to give their fathers. None of those who have treated Me with contempt will see it.
bsb.14:24: But because My servant Caleb has a different spirit and has followed Me wholeheartedly, I will bring him into the land he has entered, and his descendants will inherit it.
bsb.14:25: Now since the Amalekites and Canaanites are living in the valleys, turn back tomorrow and head for the wilderness along the route to the Red Sea.”
bsb.14:26: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
bsb.14:27: “How long will this wicked congregation grumble against Me? I have heard the complaints that the Israelites are making against Me.
bsb.14:28: So tell them: As surely as I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you exactly as I heard you say.
bsb.14:29: Your bodies will fall in this wilderness—all who were numbered in the census, everyone twenty years of age or older—because you have grumbled against Me.
bsb.14:30: Surely none of you will enter the land in which I swore to settle you, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
bsb.14:31: But I will bring your children, whom you said would become plunder, into the land you have rejected—and they will enjoy it.
bsb.14:32: As for you, however, your bodies will fall in this wilderness.
bsb.14:33: Your children will be shepherds in the wilderness for forty years, and they will suffer for your unfaithfulness until the last of your bodies lies in the wilderness.
bsb.14:34: In keeping with the forty days you spied out the land, you shall bear your guilt forty years—a year for each day—and you will experience My alienation.
bsb.14:35: I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will surely do these things to this entire wicked congregation, which has conspired against Me. They will meet their end in the wilderness, and there they will die.”
bsb.14:36: So the men Moses had sent to spy out the land, who had returned and made the whole congregation grumble against him by bringing out a bad report about the land—
bsb.14:37: those men who had brought out the bad report about the land—were struck down by a plague before the LORD.
bsb.14:38: Of those men who had gone to spy out the land, only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive.
bsb.14:39: And when Moses relayed these words to all the Israelites, the people mourned bitterly.
bsb.14:40: Early the next morning they got up and went up toward the ridge of the hill country. “We have indeed sinned,” they said, “but we will go to the place the LORD has promised.”
bsb.14:41: But Moses said, “Why are you transgressing the commandment of the LORD? This will not succeed!
bsb.14:42: Do not go up, lest you be struck down by your enemies, because the LORD is not among you.
bsb.14:43: For there the Amalekites and Canaanites will face you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned away from the LORD, He will not be with you.”
bsb.14:44: But they dared to go up to the ridge of the hill country, though neither Moses nor the ark of the covenant of the LORD moved from the camp.
bsb.14:45: Then the Amalekites and Canaanites who lived in that part of the hill country came down, attacked them, and routed them all the way to Hormah.
bsb.15:1: Then the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.15:2: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: After you enter the land that I am giving you as a home
bsb.15:3: and you present an offering made by fire to the LORD from the herd or flock to produce a pleasing aroma to the LORD—either a burnt offering or a sacrifice, for a special vow or freewill offering or appointed feast—
bsb.15:4: then the one presenting his offering to the LORD shall also present a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter hin of olive oil.
bsb.15:5: With the burnt offering or sacrifice of each lamb, you are to prepare a quarter hin of wine as a drink offering.
bsb.15:6: With a ram you are to prepare a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of olive oil,
bsb.15:7: and a third of a hin of wine as a drink offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
bsb.15:8: When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or sacrifice to fulfill a vow or as a peace offering to the LORD,
bsb.15:9: present with the bull a grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of olive oil.
bsb.15:10: Also present half a hin of wine as a drink offering. It is an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
bsb.15:11: This is to be done for each bull, ram, lamb, or goat.
bsb.15:12: This is how you must prepare each one, no matter how many.
bsb.15:13: Everyone who is native-born shall prepare these things in this way when he presents an offering made by fire as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
bsb.15:14: And for the generations to come, if a foreigner residing with you or someone else among you wants to prepare an offering made by fire as a pleasing aroma to the LORD, he is to do exactly as you do.
bsb.15:15: The assembly is to have the same statute both for you and for the foreign resident; it is a permanent statute for the generations to come. You and the foreigner shall be the same before the LORD.
bsb.15:16: The same law and the same ordinance will apply both to you and to the foreigner residing with you.”
bsb.15:17: Then the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.15:18: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land to which I am bringing you
bsb.15:19: and you eat the food of the land, you shall lift up an offering to the LORD.
bsb.15:20: From the first of your dough, you are to lift up a cake as a contribution; offer it just like an offering from the threshing floor.
bsb.15:21: Throughout your generations, you are to give the LORD an offering from the first of your dough.
bsb.15:22: Now if you stray unintentionally and do not obey all these commandments that the LORD has spoken to Moses—
bsb.15:23: all that the LORD has commanded you through Moses from the day the LORD gave them and continuing through the generations to come—
bsb.15:24: and if it was done unintentionally without the knowledge of the congregation, then the whole congregation is to prepare one young bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, with its grain offering and drink offering according to the regulation, and one male goat as a sin offering.
bsb.15:25: The priest is to make atonement for the whole congregation of Israel, so that they may be forgiven; for the sin was unintentional and they have brought to the LORD an offering made by fire and a sin offering, presented before the LORD for their unintentional sin.
bsb.15:26: Then the whole congregation of Israel and the foreigners residing among them will be forgiven, since it happened to all the people unintentionally.
bsb.15:27: Also, if one person sins unintentionally, he is to present a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
bsb.15:28: And the priest shall make atonement before the LORD on behalf of the person who erred by sinning unintentionally; and when atonement has been made for him, he will be forgiven.
bsb.15:29: You shall have the same law for the one who acts in error, whether he is a native-born Israelite or a foreigner residing among you.
bsb.15:30: But the person who sins defiantly, whether a native or foreigner, blasphemes the LORD. That person shall be cut off from among his people.
bsb.15:31: He shall certainly be cut off, because he has despised the word of the LORD and broken His commandment; his guilt remains on him.”
bsb.15:32: While the Israelites were in the wilderness, a man was found gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
bsb.15:33: Those who found the man gathering wood brought him to Moses, Aaron, and the whole congregation,
bsb.15:34: and because it had not been declared what should be done to him, they placed him in custody.
bsb.15:35: And the LORD said to Moses, “The man must surely be put to death. The whole congregation is to stone him outside the camp.”
bsb.15:36: So the whole congregation took the man outside the camp and stoned him to death, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
bsb.15:37: Later, the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.15:38: “Speak to the Israelites and tell them that throughout the generations to come they are to make for themselves tassels for the corners of their garments, with a blue cord on each tassel.
bsb.15:39: These will serve as tassels for you to look at, so that you may remember all the commandments of the LORD, that you may obey them and not prostitute yourselves by following your own heart and your own eyes.
bsb.15:40: Then you will remember and obey all My commandments, and you will be holy to your God.
bsb.15:41: I am the LORD your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God.”
bsb.16:1: Now Korah son of Izhar, the son of Kohath son of Levi, along with some Reubenites—Dathan and Abiram, sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth—conducted
bsb.16:2: a rebellion against Moses, along with 250 men of Israel renowned as leaders of the congregation and representatives in the assembly.
bsb.16:3: They came together against Moses and Aaron and told them, “You have taken too much upon yourselves! For everyone in the entire congregation is holy, and the LORD is in their midst. Why then do you exalt yourselves above the assembly of the LORD?”
bsb.16:4: When Moses heard this, he fell facedown.
bsb.16:5: Then he said to Korah and all his followers, “Tomorrow morning the LORD will reveal who belongs to Him and who is holy, and He will bring that person near to Himself. The one He chooses, He will bring near to Himself.
bsb.16:6: You, Korah, and all your followers are to do as follows: Take censers,
bsb.16:7: and tomorrow you are to place fire and incense in them in the presence of the LORD. Then the man the LORD chooses will be the one who is holy. It is you sons of Levi who have taken too much upon yourselves!”
bsb.16:8: Moses also said to Korah, “Now listen, you sons of Levi!
bsb.16:9: Is it not enough for you that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel and brought you near to Himself to perform the work at the LORD’s tabernacle, and to stand before the congregation to minister to them?
bsb.16:10: He has brought you near, you and all your fellow Levites, but you are seeking the priesthood as well.
bsb.16:11: Therefore, it is you and all your followers who have conspired against the LORD! As for Aaron, who is he that you should grumble against him?”
bsb.16:12: Then Moses summoned Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they said, “We will not come!
bsb.16:13: Is it not enough that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness? Must you also appoint yourself as ruler over us?
bsb.16:14: Moreover, you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey or given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Will you gouge out the eyes of these men? No, we will not come!”
bsb.16:15: Then Moses became very angry and said to the LORD, “Do not regard their offering. I have not taken one donkey from them or mistreated a single one of them.”
bsb.16:16: And Moses said to Korah, “You and all your followers are to appear before the LORD tomorrow—you and they and Aaron.
bsb.16:17: Each man is to take his censer, place incense in it, and present it before the LORD—250 censers. You and Aaron are to present your censers as well.”
bsb.16:18: So each man took his censer, put fire and incense in it, and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
bsb.16:19: When Korah had gathered his whole assembly against them at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, the glory of the LORD appeared to the whole congregation.
bsb.16:20: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
bsb.16:21: “Separate yourselves from this congregation so that I may consume them in an instant.”
bsb.16:22: But Moses and Aaron fell facedown and said, “O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, when one man sins, will You be angry with the whole congregation?”
bsb.16:23: Then the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.16:24: “Tell the congregation to move away from the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
bsb.16:25: So Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him.
bsb.16:26: And he warned the congregation, “Move away now from the tents of these wicked men. Do not touch anything that belongs to them, or you will be swept away because of all their sins.”
bsb.16:27: So they moved away from the dwellings of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. Meanwhile, Dathan and Abiram had come out and stood at the entrances to their tents with their wives and children and infants.
bsb.16:28: Then Moses said, “This is how you will know that the LORD has sent me to do all these things, for it was not my own doing:
bsb.16:29: If these men die a natural death, or if they suffer the fate of all men, then the LORD has not sent me.
bsb.16:30: But if the LORD brings about something unprecedented, and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them and all that belongs to them so that they go down alive into Sheol, then you will know that these men have treated the LORD with contempt.”
bsb.16:31: As soon as Moses had finished saying all this, the ground beneath them split open,
bsb.16:32: and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households—all Korah’s men and all their possessions.
bsb.16:33: They went down alive into Sheol with all they owned. The earth closed over them, and they vanished from the assembly.
bsb.16:34: At their cries, all the people of Israel who were around them fled, saying, “The earth may swallow us too!”
bsb.16:35: And fire came forth from the LORD and consumed the 250 men who were offering the incense.
bsb.16:36: Then the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.16:37: “Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to remove the censers from the flames and to scatter the coals far away, because the censers are holy.
bsb.16:38: As for the censers of those who sinned at the cost of their own lives, hammer them into sheets to overlay the altar, for these were presented before the LORD, and so have become holy. They will serve as a sign to the Israelites.”
bsb.16:39: So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers brought by those who had been burned up, and he had them hammered out to overlay the altar,
bsb.16:40: just as the LORD commanded him through Moses. This was to be a reminder to the Israelites that no outsider who is not a descendant of Aaron should approach to offer incense before the LORD, lest he become like Korah and his followers.
bsb.16:41: The next day the whole congregation of Israel grumbled against Moses and Aaron, saying, “You have killed the LORD’s people!”
bsb.16:42: But when the congregation gathered against them, Moses and Aaron turned toward the Tent of Meeting, and suddenly the cloud covered it and the glory of the LORD appeared.
bsb.16:43: Then Moses and Aaron went to the front of the Tent of Meeting,
bsb.16:44: and the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.16:45: “Get away from this congregation so that I may consume them in an instant.” And Moses and Aaron fell facedown.
bsb.16:46: Moses said to Aaron, “Take your censer, place fire from the altar in it, and add incense. Go quickly to the congregation and make atonement for them, because wrath has come out from the LORD; the plague has begun.”
bsb.16:47: So Aaron took the censer as Moses had ordered and ran into the midst of the assembly. And seeing that the plague had begun among the people, he offered the incense and made atonement for the people.
bsb.16:48: He stood between the living and the dead, and the plague was halted.
bsb.16:49: But those who died from the plague numbered 14,700, in addition to those who had died on account of Korah.
bsb.16:50: Then Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, since the plague had been halted.
bsb.17:1: And the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.17:2: “Speak to the Israelites and take from them twelve staffs, one from the leader of each tribe. Write each man’s name on his staff,
bsb.17:3: and write Aaron’s name on the staff of Levi, because there must be one staff for the head of each tribe.
bsb.17:4: Place the staffs in the Tent of Meeting in front of the Testimony, where I meet with you.
bsb.17:5: The staff belonging to the man I choose will sprout, and I will rid Myself of the constant grumbling of the Israelites against you.”
bsb.17:6: So Moses spoke to the Israelites, and each of their leaders gave him a staff—one for each of the leaders of their tribes, twelve staffs in all. And Aaron’s staff was among them.
bsb.17:7: Then Moses placed the staffs before the LORD in the Tent of the Testimony.
bsb.17:8: The next day Moses entered the Tent of the Testimony and saw that Aaron’s staff, representing the house of Levi, had sprouted, put forth buds, blossomed, and produced almonds.
bsb.17:9: Then Moses brought out all the staffs from the LORD’s presence to all the Israelites. They saw them, and each man took his own staff.
bsb.17:10: The LORD said to Moses, “Put Aaron’s staff back in front of the Testimony, to be kept as a sign for the rebellious, so that you may put an end to their grumbling against Me, lest they die.”
bsb.17:11: So Moses did as the LORD had commanded him.
bsb.17:12: Then the Israelites declared to Moses, “Look, we are perishing! We are lost; we are all lost!
bsb.17:13: Anyone who comes near the tabernacle of the LORD will die. Are we all going to perish?”
bsb.18:1: So the LORD said to Aaron, “You and your sons and your father’s house must bear the iniquity involving the sanctuary. And you and your sons alone must bear the iniquity involving your priesthood.
bsb.18:2: But bring with you also your brothers from the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father, that they may join you and assist you and your sons before the Tent of the Testimony.
bsb.18:3: And they shall attend to your duties and to all the duties of the Tent; but they must not come near to the furnishings of the sanctuary or the altar, or both they and you will die.
bsb.18:4: They are to join you and attend to the duties of the Tent of Meeting, doing all the work at the Tent; but no outsider may come near you.
bsb.18:5: And you shall attend to the duties of the sanctuary and of the altar, so that wrath may not fall on the Israelites again.
bsb.18:6: Behold, I Myself have selected your fellow Levites from the Israelites as a gift to you, dedicated to the LORD to perform the service for the Tent of Meeting.
bsb.18:7: But only you and your sons shall attend to your priesthood for everything concerning the altar and what is inside the veil, and you are to perform that service. I am giving you the work of the priesthood as a gift, but any outsider who comes near the sanctuary must be put to death.”
bsb.18:8: Then the LORD said to Aaron, “Behold, I have put you in charge of My offerings. As for all the sacred offerings of the Israelites, I have given them to you and your sons as a portion and a permanent statute.
bsb.18:9: A portion of the most holy offerings reserved from the fire will be yours. From all the offerings they render to Me as most holy offerings, whether grain offerings or sin offerings or guilt offerings, that part belongs to you and your sons.
bsb.18:10: You are to eat it as a most holy offering, and every male may eat it. You shall regard it as holy.
bsb.18:11: And this is yours as well: the offering of their gifts, along with all the wave offerings of the Israelites. I have given this to you and your sons and daughters as a permanent statute. Every ceremonially clean person in your household may eat it.
bsb.18:12: I give you all the freshest olive oil and all the finest new wine and grain that the Israelites give to the LORD as their firstfruits.
bsb.18:13: The firstfruits of everything in their land that they bring to the LORD will belong to you. Every ceremonially clean person in your household may eat them.
bsb.18:14: Every devoted thing in Israel belongs to you.
bsb.18:15: The firstborn of every womb, whether man or beast, that is offered to the LORD belongs to you. But you must surely redeem every firstborn son and every firstborn male of unclean animals.
bsb.18:16: You are to pay the redemption price for a month-old male according to your valuation: five shekels of silver, according to the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.
bsb.18:17: But you must not redeem the firstborn of an ox, a sheep, or a goat; they are holy. You are to sprinkle their blood on the altar and burn their fat as an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
bsb.18:18: And their meat belongs to you, just as the breast and right thigh of the wave offering belong to you.
bsb.18:19: All the holy offerings that the Israelites present to the LORD I give to you and to your sons and daughters as a permanent statute. It is a permanent covenant of salt before the LORD for you and your offspring.”
bsb.18:20: Then the LORD said to Aaron, “You will have no inheritance in their land, nor will you have any portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.
bsb.18:21: Behold, I have given to the Levites all the tithes in Israel as an inheritance in return for the work they do, the service of the Tent of Meeting.
bsb.18:22: No longer may the Israelites come near to the Tent of Meeting, or they will incur guilt and die.
bsb.18:23: The Levites are to perform the work of the Tent of Meeting, and they must bear their iniquity. This is a permanent statute for the generations to come. The Levites will not receive an inheritance among the Israelites.
bsb.18:24: For I have given to the Levites as their inheritance the tithe that the Israelites present to the LORD as a contribution. That is why I told them that they would not receive an inheritance among the Israelites.”
bsb.18:26: “Speak to the Levites and tell them: ‘When you receive from the Israelites the tithe that I have given you as your inheritance, you must present part of it as an offering to the LORD—a tithe of the tithe.
bsb.18:27: Your offering will be reckoned to you as grain from the threshing floor or juice from the winepress.
bsb.18:28: So you are to present an offering to the LORD from all the tithes you receive from the Israelites, and from these you are to give the LORD’s offering to Aaron the priest.
bsb.18:29: You must present the offering due the LORD from all the best of every gift, the holiest part of it.’
bsb.18:30: Therefore say to the Levites, ‘When you have presented the best part, it will be reckoned to you as the produce of the threshing floor or winepress.
bsb.18:31: And you and your households may eat the rest of it anywhere; it is the compensation for your work at the Tent of Meeting.
bsb.18:32: Once you have presented the best part of it, you will not incur guilt because of it. But you must not defile the sacred offerings of the Israelites, or else you will die.’”
bsb.19:1: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
bsb.19:2: “This is the statute of the law that the LORD has commanded: Instruct the Israelites to bring you an unblemished red heifer that has no defect and has never been placed under a yoke.
bsb.19:3: Give it to Eleazar the priest, and he will have it brought outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence.
bsb.19:4: Eleazar the priest is to take some of its blood on his finger and sprinkle it seven times toward the front of the Tent of Meeting.
bsb.19:5: Then the heifer must be burned in his sight. Its hide, its flesh, and its blood are to be burned, along with its dung.
bsb.19:6: The priest is to take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet wool and throw them onto the burning heifer.
bsb.19:7: Then the priest must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water; after that he may enter the camp, but he will be ceremonially unclean until evening.
bsb.19:8: The one who burned the heifer must also wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he too will be ceremonially unclean until evening.
bsb.19:9: Then a man who is ceremonially clean is to gather up the ashes of the heifer and store them in a ceremonially clean place outside the camp. They must be kept by the congregation of Israel for preparing the water of purification; this is for purification from sin.
bsb.19:10: The man who has gathered up the ashes of the heifer must also wash his clothes, and he will be ceremonially unclean until evening. This is a permanent statute for the Israelites and for the foreigner residing among them.
bsb.19:11: Whoever touches any dead body will be unclean for seven days.
bsb.19:12: He must purify himself with the water on the third day and on the seventh day; then he will be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third and seventh days, he will not be clean.
bsb.19:13: Anyone who touches a human corpse and fails to purify himself defiles the tabernacle of the LORD. That person must be cut off from Israel. He remains unclean, because the water of purification has not been sprinkled on him, and his uncleanness is still on him.
bsb.19:14: This is the law when a person dies in a tent: Everyone who enters the tent and everyone already in the tent will be unclean for seven days,
bsb.19:15: and any open container without a lid fastened on it is unclean.
bsb.19:16: Anyone in the open field who touches someone who has been killed by the sword or has died of natural causes, or anyone who touches a human bone or a grave, will be unclean for seven days.
bsb.19:17: For the purification of the unclean person, take some of the ashes of the burnt sin offering, put them in a jar, and pour fresh water over them.
bsb.19:18: Then a man who is ceremonially clean is to take some hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle the tent, all the furnishings, and the people who were there. He is also to sprinkle the one who touched a bone, a grave, or a person who has died or been slain.
bsb.19:19: The man who is ceremonially clean is to sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. After he purifies the unclean person on the seventh day, the one being cleansed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and that evening he will be clean.
bsb.19:20: But if a person who is unclean does not purify himself, he will be cut off from the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD. The water of purification has not been sprinkled on him; he is unclean.
bsb.19:21: This is a permanent statute for the people: The one who sprinkles the water of purification must wash his clothes, and whoever touches the water of purification will be unclean until evening.
bsb.19:22: Anything the unclean person touches will become unclean, and anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening.”
bsb.20:1: In the first month, the whole congregation of Israel entered the Wilderness of Zin and stayed in Kadesh. There Miriam died and was buried.
bsb.20:2: Now there was no water for the congregation, so they gathered against Moses and Aaron.
bsb.20:3: The people quarreled with Moses and said, “If only we had perished with our brothers before the LORD!
bsb.20:4: Why have you brought the LORD’s assembly into this wilderness for us and our livestock to die here?
bsb.20:5: Why have you led us up out of Egypt to bring us to this wretched place? It is not a place of grain, figs, vines, or pomegranates—and there is no water to drink!”
bsb.20:6: Then Moses and Aaron went from the presence of the assembly to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. They fell facedown, and the glory of the LORD appeared to them.
bsb.20:7: And the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.20:8: “Take the staff and assemble the congregation. You and your brother Aaron are to speak to the rock while they watch, and it will pour out its water. You will bring out water from the rock and provide drink for the congregation and their livestock.”
bsb.20:9: So Moses took the staff from the LORD’s presence, just as he had been commanded.
bsb.20:10: Then Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly in front of the rock, and Moses said to them, “Listen now, you rebels, must we bring you water out of this rock?”
bsb.20:11: Then Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff, so that a great amount of water gushed out, and the congregation and their livestock were able to drink.
bsb.20:12: But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you did not trust Me to show My holiness in the sight of the Israelites, you will not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them.”
bsb.20:13: These were the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites quarreled with the LORD, and He showed His holiness among them.
bsb.20:14: From Kadesh, Moses sent messengers to tell the king of Edom, “This is what your brother Israel says: You know all the hardship that has befallen us,
bsb.20:15: how our fathers went down to Egypt, where we lived many years. The Egyptians mistreated us and our fathers,
bsb.20:16: and when we cried out to the LORD, He heard our voice, sent an angel, and brought us out of Egypt. Now look, we are in Kadesh, a city on the edge of your territory.
bsb.20:17: Please let us pass through your land. We will not cut through any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well. We will stay on the King’s Highway; we will not turn to the right or to the left until we have passed through your territory.”
bsb.20:18: But Edom answered, “You may not travel through our land, or we will come out and confront you with the sword.”
bsb.20:19: “We will stay on the main road,” the Israelites replied, “and if we or our herds drink your water, we will pay for it. There will be no problem; only let us pass through on foot.”
bsb.20:20: But Edom insisted, “You may not pass through.” And they came out to confront the Israelites with a large army and a strong hand.
bsb.20:21: So Edom refused to allow Israel to pass through their territory, and Israel turned away from them.
bsb.20:22: After they had set out from Kadesh, the whole congregation of Israel came to Mount Hor.
bsb.20:23: And at Mount Hor, near the border of the land of Edom, the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
bsb.20:24: “Aaron will be gathered to his people; he will not enter the land that I have given the Israelites, because both of you rebelled against My command at the waters of Meribah.
bsb.20:25: Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor.
bsb.20:26: Remove Aaron’s priestly garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will be gathered to his people and will die there.”
bsb.20:27: So Moses did as the LORD had commanded, and they climbed Mount Hor in the sight of the whole congregation.
bsb.20:28: After Moses had removed Aaron’s garments and put them on his son Eleazar, Aaron died there on top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
bsb.20:29: When the whole congregation saw that Aaron had died, the entire house of Israel mourned for him thirty days.
bsb.21:1: When the Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming along the road to Atharim, he attacked Israel and captured some prisoners.
bsb.21:2: So Israel made a vow to the LORD: “If You will deliver this people into our hands, we will devote their cities to destruction.”
bsb.21:3: And the LORD heard Israel’s plea and delivered up the Canaanites. Israel devoted them and their cities to destruction; so they named the place Hormah.
bsb.21:4: Then they set out from Mount Hor along the route to the Red Sea, in order to bypass the land of Edom. But the people grew impatient on the journey
bsb.21:5: and spoke against God and against Moses: “Why have you led us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread or water, and we detest this wretched food!”
bsb.21:6: So the LORD sent venomous snakes among the people, and many of the Israelites were bitten and died.
bsb.21:7: Then the people came to Moses and said, “We have sinned by speaking against the LORD and against you. Intercede with the LORD so He will take the snakes away from us.” So Moses interceded for the people.
bsb.21:8: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Make a fiery serpent and mount it on a pole. When anyone who is bitten looks at it, he will live.”
bsb.21:9: So Moses made a bronze snake and mounted it on a pole. If anyone who was bitten looked at the bronze snake, he would live.
bsb.21:10: Then the Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.
bsb.21:11: They journeyed from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim in the wilderness opposite Moab to the east.
bsb.21:12: From there they set out and camped in the Valley of Zered.
bsb.21:13: From there they moved on and camped on the other side of the Arnon, in the wilderness that extends into the Amorite territory. Now the Arnon is the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
bsb.21:14: Therefore it is stated in the Book of the Wars of the LORD: “Waheb in Suphah and the wadis of the Arnon,
bsb.21:15: even the slopes of the wadis that extend to the site of Ar and lie along the border of Moab.”
bsb.21:16: From there they went on to Beer, the well where the LORD said to Moses, “Gather the people so that I may give them water.”
bsb.21:17: Then Israel sang this song: “Spring up, O well, all of you sing to it!
bsb.21:18: The princes dug the well; the nobles of the people hollowed it out with their scepters and with their staffs.” From the wilderness the Israelites went on to Mattanah,
bsb.21:19: and from Mattanah to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth,
bsb.21:20: and from Bamoth to the valley in Moab where the top of Pisgah overlooks the wasteland.
bsb.21:21: Then Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,
bsb.21:22: “Let us pass through your land. We will not cut through any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well. We will stay on the King’s Highway until we have passed through your territory.”
bsb.21:23: But Sihon would not let Israel pass through his territory. Instead, he gathered his whole army and went out to confront Israel in the wilderness. When he came to Jahaz, he fought against Israel.
bsb.21:24: And Israel put him to the sword and took possession of his land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok—but only up to the border of the Ammonites, because it was fortified.
bsb.21:25: Israel captured all the cities of the Amorites and occupied them, including Heshbon and all its villages.
bsb.21:26: Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites, who had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land as far as the Arnon.
bsb.21:27: That is why the poets say: “Come to Heshbon, let it be rebuilt; let the city of Sihon be restored.
bsb.21:28: For a fire went out from Heshbon, a blaze from the city of Sihon. It consumed Ar of Moab, the rulers of Arnon’s heights.
bsb.21:29: Woe to you, O Moab! You are destroyed, O people of Chemosh! He gave up his sons as refugees, and his daughters into captivity to Sihon king of the Amorites.
bsb.21:30: But we have overthrown them; Heshbon is destroyed as far as Dibon. We demolished them as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba.”
bsb.21:31: So Israel lived in the land of the Amorites.
bsb.21:32: After Moses had sent spies to Jazer, Israel captured its villages and drove out the Amorites who were there.
bsb.21:33: Then they turned and went up the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan and his whole army came out to meet them in battle at Edrei.
bsb.21:34: But the LORD said to Moses, “Do not fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand, along with all his people and his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”
bsb.21:35: So they struck down Og, along with his sons and his whole army, until no remnant was left. And they took possession of his land.
bsb.22:1: Then the Israelites traveled on and camped in the plains of Moab near the Jordan, across from Jericho.
bsb.22:2: Now Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites,
bsb.22:3: and Moab was terrified of the people because they were numerous. Indeed, Moab dreaded the Israelites.
bsb.22:4: So the Moabites said to the elders of Midian, “This horde will devour everything around us, as an ox licks up the grass of the field.” Since Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time,
bsb.22:5: he sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor at Pethor, which is by the Euphrates in the land of his people. “Behold, a people has come out of Egypt,” said Balak. “They cover the face of the land and have settled next to me.
bsb.22:6: So please come now and put a curse on this people, because they are too mighty for me. Perhaps I may be able to defeat them and drive them out of the land; for I know that those you bless are blessed, and those you curse are cursed.”
bsb.22:7: The elders of Moab and Midian departed with the fees for divination in hand. They came to Balaam and relayed to him the words of Balak.
bsb.22:8: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and I will give you the answer that the LORD speaks to me.” So the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.
bsb.22:9: Then God came to Balaam and asked, “Who are these men with you?”
bsb.22:10: And Balaam said to God, “Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent me this message:
bsb.22:11: ‘Behold, a people has come out of Egypt, and they cover the face of the land. Now come and put a curse on them for me. Perhaps I may be able to fight against them and drive them away.’”
bsb.22:12: But God said to Balaam, “Do not go with them. You are not to curse this people, for they are blessed.”
bsb.22:13: So Balaam got up the next morning and said to Balak’s princes, “Go back to your homeland, because the LORD has refused to let me go with you.”
bsb.22:14: And the princes of Moab arose, returned to Balak, and said, “Balaam refused to come with us.”
bsb.22:15: Then Balak sent other princes, more numerous and more distinguished than the first messengers.
bsb.22:16: They came to Balaam and said, “This is what Balak son of Zippor says: ‘Please let nothing hinder you from coming to me,
bsb.22:17: for I will honor you richly and do whatever you say. So please come and put a curse on this people for me!’”
bsb.22:18: But Balaam replied to the servants of Balak, “If Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not do anything small or great to go beyond the command of the LORD my God.
bsb.22:19: So now, please stay here overnight as the others did, that I may find out what else the LORD has to tell me.”
bsb.22:20: That night God came to Balaam and said, “Since these men have come to summon you, get up and go with them, but you must only do what I tell you.”
bsb.22:21: So in the morning Balaam got up, saddled his donkey, and went with the princes of Moab.
bsb.22:22: Then God’s anger was kindled because Balaam was going along, and the angel of the LORD stood in the road to oppose him. Balaam was riding his donkey, and his two servants were with him.
bsb.22:23: When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand, she turned off the path and went into a field. So Balaam beat her to return her to the path.
bsb.22:24: Then the angel of the LORD stood in a narrow passage between two vineyards, with walls on either side.
bsb.22:25: And the donkey saw the angel of the LORD and pressed herself against the wall, crushing Balaam’s foot against it. So he beat her once again.
bsb.22:26: And the angel of the LORD moved on ahead and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn to the right or left.
bsb.22:27: When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she lay down under Balaam, and he became furious and beat her with his staff.
bsb.22:28: Then the LORD opened the donkey’s mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?”
bsb.22:29: Balaam answered the donkey, “You have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now!”
bsb.22:30: But the donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not the donkey you have ridden all your life until today? Have I ever treated you this way before?” “No,” he replied.
bsb.22:31: Then the LORD opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand. And Balaam bowed low and fell facedown.
bsb.22:32: The angel of the LORD asked him, “Why have you beaten your donkey these three times? Behold, I have come out to oppose you, because your way is perverse before me.
bsb.22:33: The donkey saw me and turned away from me these three times. If she had not turned away, then by now I would surely have killed you and let her live.”
bsb.22:34: “I have sinned,” Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, “for I did not realize that you were standing in the road to confront me. And now, if this is displeasing in your sight, I will go back home.”
bsb.22:35: But the angel of the LORD said to Balaam, “Go with the men, but you are to speak only what I tell you.” So Balaam went with the princes of Balak.
bsb.22:36: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at the Moabite city on the Arnon border, at the edge of his territory.
bsb.22:37: And he said to Balaam, “Did I not send you an urgent summons? Why did you not come to me? Am I really not able to richly reward you?”
bsb.22:38: “See, I have come to you,” Balaam replied, “but can I say just anything? I must speak only the word that God puts in my mouth.”
bsb.22:39: So Balaam accompanied Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.
bsb.22:40: Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep, and he gave portions to Balaam and the princes who were with him.
bsb.22:41: The next morning, Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal. From there he could see the outskirts of the camp of the people.
bsb.23:1: Then Balaam said to Balak, “Build for me seven altars here, and prepare for me seven bulls and seven rams.”
bsb.23:2: So Balak did as Balaam had instructed, and Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
bsb.23:3: “Stay here by your burnt offering while I am gone,” Balaam said to Balak. “Perhaps the LORD will meet with me. And whatever He reveals to me, I will tell you.” So Balaam went off to a barren height,
bsb.23:4: and God met with him. “I have set up seven altars,” Balaam said, “and on each altar I have offered a bull and a ram.”
bsb.23:5: Then the LORD put a message in Balaam’s mouth, saying, “Return to Balak and give him this message.”
bsb.23:6: So he returned to Balak, who was standing there beside his burnt offering, with all the princes of Moab.
bsb.23:7: And Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying: “Balak brought me from Aram, the king of Moab from the mountains of the east. ‘Come,’ he said, ‘put a curse on Jacob for me; come and denounce Israel!’
bsb.23:8: How can I curse what God has not cursed? How can I denounce what the LORD has not denounced?
bsb.23:9: For I see them from atop the rocky cliffs, and I watch them from the hills. Behold, a people dwelling apart, not reckoning themselves among the nations.
bsb.23:10: Who can count the dust of Jacob or number even a fourth of Israel? Let me die the death of the righteous; let my end be like theirs!”
bsb.23:11: Then Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I brought you here to curse my enemies, and behold, you have only blessed them!”
bsb.23:12: But Balaam replied, “Should I not speak exactly what the LORD puts in my mouth?”
bsb.23:13: Then Balak said to him, “Please come with me to another place where you can see them. You will only see the outskirts of their camp—not all of them. And from there, curse them for me.”
bsb.23:14: So Balak took him to the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, where he built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
bsb.23:15: Balaam said to Balak, “Stay here beside your burnt offering while I meet the LORD over there.”
bsb.23:16: And the LORD met with Balaam and put a message in his mouth, saying, “Return to Balak and speak what I tell you.”
bsb.23:17: So he returned to Balak, who was standing there by his burnt offering with the princes of Moab. “What did the LORD say?” Balak asked.
bsb.23:18: Then Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying: “Arise, O Balak, and listen; give ear to me, O son of Zippor.
bsb.23:19: God is not a man, that He should lie, or a son of man, that He should change His mind. Does He speak and not act? Does He promise and not fulfill?
bsb.23:20: I have indeed received a command to bless; He has blessed, and I cannot change it.
bsb.23:21: He considers no disaster for Jacob; He sees no trouble for Israel. The LORD their God is with them, and the shout of the King is among them.
bsb.23:22: God brought them out of Egypt with strength like a wild ox.
bsb.23:23: For there is no spell against Jacob and no divination against Israel. It will now be said of Jacob and Israel, ‘What great things God has done!’
bsb.23:24: Behold, the people rise like a lioness; they rouse themselves like a lion, not resting until they devour their prey and drink the blood of the slain.”
bsb.23:25: Now Balak said to Balaam, “Then neither curse them at all nor bless them at all!”
bsb.23:26: But Balaam replied, “Did I not tell you that whatever the LORD says, I must do?”
bsb.23:27: “Please come,” said Balak, “I will take you to another place. Perhaps it will please God that you curse them for me from there.”
bsb.23:28: And Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooks the wasteland.
bsb.23:29: Then Balaam said, “Build for me seven altars here, and prepare for me seven bulls and seven rams.”
bsb.23:30: So Balak did as Balaam had instructed, and he offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
bsb.24:1: And when Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not resort to sorcery as on previous occasions, but he turned his face toward the wilderness.
bsb.24:2: When Balaam looked up and saw Israel encamped tribe by tribe, the Spirit of God came upon him,
bsb.24:3: and he lifted up an oracle, saying: “This is the prophecy of Balaam son of Beor, the prophecy of a man whose eyes are open,
bsb.24:4: the prophecy of one who hears the words of God, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who bows down with eyes wide open:
bsb.24:5: How lovely are your tents, O Jacob, your dwellings, O Israel!
bsb.24:6: They spread out like palm groves, like gardens beside a stream, like aloes the LORD has planted, like cedars beside the waters.
bsb.24:7: Water will flow from his buckets, and his seed will have abundant water. His king will be greater than Agag, and his kingdom will be exalted.
bsb.24:8: God brought him out of Egypt with strength like a wild ox, to devour hostile nations and crush their bones, to pierce them with arrows.
bsb.24:9: He crouches, he lies down like a lion; like a lioness, who dares to rouse him? Blessed are those who bless you and cursed are those who curse you.”
bsb.24:10: Then Balak’s anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together and said to Balaam, “I summoned you to curse my enemies, but behold, you have persisted in blessing them these three times.
bsb.24:11: Therefore, flee at once to your home! I said I would richly reward you, but instead the LORD has denied your reward.”
bsb.24:12: Balaam answered Balak, “Did I not already tell the messengers you sent me
bsb.24:13: that even if Balak were to give me his house full of silver and gold, I could not do anything of my own accord, good or bad, to go beyond the command of the LORD? I will speak whatever the LORD says.
bsb.24:14: Now I am going back to my people, but come, let me warn you what this people will do to your people in the days to come.”
bsb.24:15: Then Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying, “This is the prophecy of Balaam son of Beor, the prophecy of a man whose eyes are open,
bsb.24:16: the prophecy of one who hears the words of God, who has knowledge from the Most High, who sees a vision from the Almighty, who bows down with eyes wide open:
bsb.24:17: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star will come forth from Jacob, and a scepter will arise from Israel. He will crush the skulls of Moab and strike down all the sons of Sheth.
bsb.24:18: Edom will become a possession, as will Seir, his enemy; but Israel will perform with valor.
bsb.24:19: A ruler will come from Jacob and destroy the survivors of the city.”
bsb.24:20: Then Balaam saw Amalek and lifted up an oracle, saying: “Amalek was first among the nations, but his end is destruction.”
bsb.24:21: Next he saw the Kenites and lifted up an oracle, saying: “Your dwelling place is secure, and your nest is set in a cliff.
bsb.24:22: Yet Kain will be destroyed when Asshur takes you captive.”
bsb.24:23: Once more Balaam lifted up an oracle, saying: “Ah, who can live unless God has ordained it?
bsb.24:24: Ships will come from the coasts of Cyprus; they will subdue Asshur and Eber, but they too will perish forever.”
bsb.24:25: Then Balaam arose and returned to his homeland, and Balak also went on his way.
bsb.25:1: While Israel was staying in Shittim, the men began to indulge in sexual immorality with the daughters of Moab,
bsb.25:2: who also invited them to the sacrifices for their gods. And the people ate and bowed down to these gods.
bsb.25:3: So Israel joined in worshiping Baal of Peor, and the anger of the LORD burned against them.
bsb.25:4: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Take all the leaders of the people and execute them in broad daylight before the LORD, so that His fierce anger may turn away from Israel.”
bsb.25:5: So Moses told the judges of Israel, “Each of you must kill all of his men who have joined in worshiping Baal of Peor.”
bsb.25:6: Just then an Israelite man brought to his family a Midianite woman in the sight of Moses and the whole congregation of Israel while they were weeping at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
bsb.25:7: On seeing this, Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, got up from the assembly, took a spear in his hand,
bsb.25:8: followed the Israelite into his tent, and drove the spear through both of them—through the Israelite and on through the belly of the woman. So the plague against the Israelites was halted,
bsb.25:9: but those who died in the plague numbered 24,000.
bsb.25:10: Then the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.25:11: “Phinehas son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned My wrath away from the Israelites; for he was zealous for My sake among them, so that I did not consume the Israelites in My zeal.
bsb.25:12: Declare, therefore, that I am granting him My covenant of peace.
bsb.25:13: It will be a covenant of permanent priesthood for him and his descendants, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites.”
bsb.25:14: The name of the Israelite who was slain with the Midianite woman was Zimri son of Salu, the leader of a Simeonite family.
bsb.25:15: And the name of the slain Midianite woman was Cozbi, the daughter of Zur, a tribal chief of a Midianite family.
bsb.25:16: And the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.25:17: “Attack the Midianites and strike them dead.
bsb.25:18: For they assailed you deceitfully when they seduced you in the matter of Peor and their sister Cozbi, the daughter of the Midianite leader, the woman who was killed on the day the plague came because of Peor.”
bsb.26:1: After the plague had ended, the LORD said to Moses and Eleazar son of Aaron the priest,
bsb.26:2: “Take a census of the whole congregation of Israel by the houses of their fathers—all those twenty years of age or older who can serve in the army of Israel.”
bsb.26:3: So on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho, Moses and Eleazar the priest issued the instruction,
bsb.26:4: “Take a census of the men twenty years of age or older, as the LORD has commanded Moses.” And these were the Israelites who came out of the land of Egypt:
bsb.26:5: Reuben was the firstborn of Israel. These were the descendants of Reuben: The Hanochite clan from Hanoch, the Palluite clan from Pallu,
bsb.26:6: the Hezronite clan from Hezron, and the Carmite clan from Carmi.
bsb.26:7: These were the clans of Reuben, and their registration numbered 43,730.
bsb.26:8: Now the son of Pallu was Eliab,
bsb.26:9: and the sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. It was Dathan and Abiram, chosen by the congregation, who fought against Moses and Aaron with the followers of Korah who rebelled against the LORD.
bsb.26:10: And the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them along with Korah, whose followers died when the fire consumed 250 men. They serve as a warning sign.
bsb.26:11: However, the line of Korah did not die out.
bsb.26:12: These were the descendants of Simeon by their clans: The Nemuelite clan from Nemuel, the Jaminite clan from Jamin, the Jachinite clan from Jachin,
bsb.26:13: the Zerahite clan from Zerah, and the Shaulite clan from Shaul.
bsb.26:14: These were the clans of Simeon, and there were 22,200 men.
bsb.26:15: These were the descendants of Gad by their clans: The Zephonite clan from Zephon, the Haggite clan from Haggi, the Shunite clan from Shuni,
bsb.26:16: the Oznite clan from Ozni, the Erite clan from Eri,
bsb.26:17: the Arodite clan from Arod, and the Arelite clan from Areli.
bsb.26:18: These were the clans of Gad, and their registration numbered 40,500.
bsb.26:19: The sons of Judah were Er and Onan, but they died in the land of Canaan.
bsb.26:20: These were the descendants of Judah by their clans: The Shelanite clan from Shelah, the Perezite clan from Perez, and the Zerahite clan from Zerah.
bsb.26:21: And these were the descendants of Perez: the Hezronite clan from Hezron and the Hamulite clan from Hamul.
bsb.26:22: These were the clans of Judah, and their registration numbered 76,500.
bsb.26:23: These were the descendants of Issachar by their clans: The Tolaite clan from Tola, the Punite clan from Puvah,
bsb.26:24: the Jashubite clan from Jashub, and the Shimronite clan from Shimron.
bsb.26:25: These were the clans of Issachar, and their registration numbered 64,300.
bsb.26:26: These were the descendants of Zebulun by their clans: The Seredite clan from Sered, the Elonite clan from Elon, and the Jahleelite clan from Jahleel.
bsb.26:27: These were the clans of Zebulun, and their registration numbered 60,500.
bsb.26:28: The descendants of Joseph included the clans of Manasseh and Ephraim.
bsb.26:29: These were the descendants of Manasseh: The Machirite clan from Machir, the father of Gilead, and the Gileadite clan from Gilead.
bsb.26:30: These were the descendants of Gilead: the Iezerite clan from Iezer, the Helekite clan from Helek,
bsb.26:31: the Asrielite clan from Asriel, the Shechemite clan from Shechem,
bsb.26:32: the Shemidaite clan from Shemida, and the Hepherite clan from Hepher.
bsb.26:33: Now Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons but only daughters. The names of his daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
bsb.26:34: These were the clans of Manasseh, and their registration numbered 52,700.
bsb.26:35: These were the descendants of Ephraim by their clans: The Shuthelahite clan from Shuthelah, the Becherite clan from Becher, and the Tahanite clan from Tahan.
bsb.26:36: And the descendants of Shuthelah were the Eranite clan from Eran.
bsb.26:37: These were the clans of Ephraim, and their registration numbered 32,500. These clans were the descendants of Joseph.
bsb.26:38: These were the descendants of Benjamin by their clans: The Belaite clan from Bela, the Ashbelite clan from Ashbel, the Ahiramite clan from Ahiram,
bsb.26:39: the Shuphamite clan from Shupham, and the Huphamite clan from Hupham.
bsb.26:40: And the descendants of Bela from Ard and Naaman were the Ardite clan from Ard and the Naamite clan from Naaman.
bsb.26:41: These were the clans of Benjamin, and their registration numbered 45,600.
bsb.26:42: These were the descendants of Dan by their clans: The Shuhamite clan from Shuham. These were the clans of Dan.
bsb.26:43: All of them were Shuhamite clans, and their registration numbered 64,400.
bsb.26:44: These were the descendants of Asher by their clans: The Imnite clan from Imnah, the Ishvite clan from Ishvi, and the Beriite clan from Beriah.
bsb.26:45: And these were the descendants of Beriah: the Heberite clan from Heber and the Malchielite clan from Malchiel.
bsb.26:46: And the name of Asher’s daughter was Serah.
bsb.26:47: These were the clans of Asher, and their registration numbered 53,400.
bsb.26:48: These were the descendants of Naphtali by their clans: The Jahzeelite clan from Jahzeel, the Gunite clan from Guni,
bsb.26:49: the Jezerite clan from Jezer, and the Shillemite clan from Shillem.
bsb.26:50: These were the clans of Naphtali, and their registration numbered 45,400.
bsb.26:51: These men of Israel numbered 601,730 in all.
bsb.26:52: Then the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.26:53: “The land is to be divided among the tribes as an inheritance, according to the number of names.
bsb.26:54: Increase the inheritance for a large tribe and decrease it for a small one; each tribe is to receive its inheritance according to the number of those registered.
bsb.26:55: Indeed, the land must be divided by lot; they shall receive their inheritance according to the names of the tribes of their fathers.
bsb.26:56: Each inheritance is to be divided by lot among the larger and smaller tribes.”
bsb.26:57: Now these were the Levites numbered by their clans: The Gershonite clan from Gershon, the Kohathite clan from Kohath, and the Merarite clan from Merari.
bsb.26:58: These were the families of the Levites: The Libnite clan, the Hebronite clan, the Mahlite clan, the Mushite clan, and the Korahite clan. Now Kohath was the father of Amram,
bsb.26:59: and Amram’s wife was named Jochebed. She was also a daughter of Levi, born to Levi in Egypt. To Amram she bore Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam.
bsb.26:60: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar were born to Aaron,
bsb.26:61: but Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD.
bsb.26:62: The registration of the Levites totaled 23,000, every male a month old or more; they were not numbered among the other Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites.
bsb.26:63: These were the ones numbered by Moses and Eleazar the priest when they counted the Israelites on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.
bsb.26:64: Among all these, however, there was not one who had been numbered by Moses and Aaron the priest when they counted the Israelites in the Wilderness of Sinai.
bsb.26:65: For the LORD had told them that they would surely die in the wilderness. Not one was left except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
bsb.27:1: Now the daughters of Zelophehad son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, belonged to the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph. These were the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. They approached
bsb.27:2: the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders, and the whole congregation, and said,
bsb.27:3: “Our father died in the wilderness, but he was not among the followers of Korah who gathered together against the LORD. Instead, he died because of his own sin, and he had no sons.
bsb.27:4: Why should the name of our father disappear from his clan because he had no sons? Give us property among our father’s brothers.”
bsb.27:5: So Moses brought their case before the LORD,
bsb.27:7: “The daughters of Zelophehad speak correctly. You certainly must give them property as an inheritance among their father’s brothers, and transfer their father’s inheritance to them.
bsb.27:8: Furthermore, you shall say to the Israelites, ‘If a man dies and leaves no son, you are to transfer his inheritance to his daughter.
bsb.27:9: If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers.
bsb.27:10: If he has no brothers, give his inheritance to his father’s brothers.
bsb.27:11: And if his father has no brothers, give his inheritance to the next of kin from his clan, that he may take possession of it. This is to be a statutory ordinance for the Israelites, as the LORD has commanded Moses.’”
bsb.27:12: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Go up this mountain of the Abarim range and see the land that I have given the Israelites.
bsb.27:13: After you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as your brother Aaron was;
bsb.27:14: for when the congregation contended in the Wilderness of Zin, both of you rebelled against My command to show My holiness in their sight regarding the waters.” Those were the waters of Meribah in Kadesh, in the Wilderness of Zin.
bsb.27:15: So Moses appealed to the LORD,
bsb.27:16: “May the LORD, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation
bsb.27:17: who will go out and come in before them, and who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the congregation of the LORD will not be like sheep without a shepherd.”
bsb.27:18: And the LORD replied to Moses, “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man with the Spirit in him, and lay your hands on him.
bsb.27:19: Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation, and commission him in their sight.
bsb.27:20: Confer on him some of your authority, so that the whole congregation of Israel will obey him.
bsb.27:21: He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who will seek counsel for him before the LORD by the judgment of the Urim. At his command, he and all the Israelites with him—the entire congregation—will go out and come in.”
bsb.27:22: Moses did as the LORD had commanded him. He took Joshua, had him stand before Eleazar the priest and the whole congregation,
bsb.27:23: and laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as the LORD had instructed through Moses.
bsb.28:1: Then the LORD said to Moses,
bsb.28:2: “Command the Israelites and say to them: See that you present to Me at its appointed time the food for My offerings by fire, as a pleasing aroma to Me.
bsb.28:3: And tell them that this is the offering made by fire you are to present to the LORD as a regular burnt offering each day: two unblemished year-old male lambs.
bsb.28:4: Offer one lamb in the morning and the other at twilight,
bsb.28:5: along with a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a grain offering, mixed with a quarter hin of oil from pressed olives.
bsb.28:6: This is a regular burnt offering established at Mount Sinai as a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
bsb.28:7: The drink offering accompanying each lamb shall be a quarter hin. Pour out the offering of fermented drink to the LORD in the sanctuary area.
bsb.28:8: And offer the second lamb at twilight, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning. It is an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
bsb.28:9: On the Sabbath day, present two unblemished year-old male lambs, accompanied by a grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, as well as a drink offering.
bsb.28:10: This is the burnt offering for every Sabbath, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
bsb.28:11: At the beginning of every month, you are to present to the LORD a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
bsb.28:12: along with three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering with each bull, two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering with the ram,
bsb.28:13: and a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering with each lamb. This is a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
bsb.28:14: Their drink offerings shall be half a hin of wine with each bull, a third of a hin with the ram, and a quarter hin with each lamb. This is the monthly burnt offering to be made at each new moon throughout the year.
bsb.28:15: In addition to the regular burnt offering with its drink offering, one male goat is to be presented to the LORD as a sin offering.
bsb.28:16: The fourteenth day of the first month is the LORD’s Passover.
bsb.28:17: On the fifteenth day of this month, there shall be a feast; for seven days unleavened bread is to be eaten.
bsb.28:18: On the first day there is to be a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work.
bsb.28:19: Present to the LORD an offering made by fire, a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished.
bsb.28:20: The grain offering shall consist of fine flour mixed with oil; offer three-tenths of an ephah with each bull, two-tenths of an ephah with the ram,
bsb.28:21: and a tenth of an ephah with each of the seven lambs.
bsb.28:22: Include one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you.
bsb.28:23: You are to present these in addition to the regular morning burnt offering.
bsb.28:24: Offer the same food each day for seven days as an offering made by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD. It is to be offered with its drink offering and the regular burnt offering.
bsb.28:25: On the seventh day you shall hold a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work.
bsb.28:26: On the day of firstfruits, when you present an offering of new grain to the LORD during the Feast of Weeks, you are to hold a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work.
bsb.28:27: Present a burnt offering of two young bulls, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old as a pleasing aroma to the LORD,
bsb.28:28: together with their grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil—three-tenths of an ephah with each bull, two-tenths of an ephah with the ram,
bsb.28:29: and a tenth of an ephah with each of the seven lambs.
bsb.28:30: Include one male goat to make atonement for you.
bsb.28:31: Offer them with their drink offerings in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering. The animals must be unblemished.
bsb.29:1: “On the first day of the seventh month, you are to hold a sacred assembly, and you must not do any regular work. This will be a day for you to sound the trumpets.
bsb.29:2: As a pleasing aroma to the LORD, you are to present a burnt offering of one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
bsb.29:3: together with their grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil—three-tenths of an ephah with the bull, two-tenths of an ephah with the ram,
bsb.29:4: and a tenth of an ephah with each of the seven male lambs.
bsb.29:5: Include one male goat as a sin offering to make atonement for you.
bsb.29:6: These are in addition to the monthly and daily burnt offerings with their prescribed grain offerings and drink offerings. They are a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to the LORD.
bsb.29:7: On the tenth day of this seventh month, you are to hold a sacred assembly, and you shall humble yourselves; you must not do any work.
bsb.29:8: Present as a pleasing aroma to the LORD a burnt offering of one young bull, one ram, and seven male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
bsb.29:9: together with their grain offerings of fine flour mixed with oil—three-tenths of an ephah with the bull, two-tenths of an ephah with the ram,
bsb.29:10: and a tenth of an ephah with each of the seven lambs.
bsb.29:11: Include one male goat for a sin offering, in addition to the sin offering of atonement and the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offerings.
bsb.29:12: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, you are to hold a sacred assembly; you must not do any regular work, and you shall observe a feast to the LORD for seven days.
bsb.29:13: As a pleasing aroma to the LORD, you are to present an offering made by fire, a burnt offering of thirteen young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
bsb.29:14: along with the grain offering of three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil with each of the thirteen bulls, two-tenths of an ephah with each of the two rams,
bsb.29:15: and a tenth of an ephah with each of the fourteen lambs.
bsb.29:16: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
bsb.29:17: On the second day you are to present twelve young bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
bsb.29:18: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.
bsb.29:19: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
bsb.29:20: On the third day you are to present eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
bsb.29:21: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.
bsb.29:22: Include one male goat as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering with its grain offering and drink offering.
bsb.29:23: On the fourth day you are to present ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen male lambs a year old, all unblemished,
bsb.29:24: along with the grain and drink offerings for the bulls, rams, and lambs, according to the number prescribed.
